description.narrative: IFC's support will enable: (i) Stakeholder effectsincreased access to finance for pensioners, including women: Kredit specializes in payroll-deducted pension loans, a segment underserved by banks due to borrower-age constraints and regulatory capital requirements. The Project will expand affordable, responsible credit for pensioners and senior women, addressing liquidity needs, healthcare expenses, and income smoothing and (ii) Stakeholder effects - Improved accessibility of financial and digital education for pensioners: The project will further support the pensioner borrowers by offering digital and financial education services specifically designed for the silver economy segment. Kredit will be part of a multi-year advisory engagement with IFC, so that pensioner clients can maximize the value received from Kredit's digital finance offering.

The proposed investment consists of a COP80,000 million own account investment (approximately $22.0 million equivalent) to the first privately placed listed social securitization in Colombia, which will be originated by Kredit Plus S.A.S. (Kredit or the Company). The securitization will have a tenor of ten years and will be issued by a special purpose vehicle (the Issuing Trust). The investment proceeds will be used to support the silver by providing loans to pensioners, 55% of which will be granted to women, in Colombia usually more credit constrained than men (a 6.9pp gap), as previously stated The total transaction size is expected to be COP160,000 million (approximately USD 44.0 million equivalent), comprising IFCs COP 80,000 million investment, mobilization of up to COP 67,200 million from private investors, and a COP 12,800 million equity tranche to be held by Kredit.
